QF.id: Income, Residential Status, Five Heads of Income_19

question.text: A "Person of Indian Origin" (PIO) for the purposes of residential status under the Income Tax Act is defined as a person:

answer.text: Whose parents were born in India after 15th August 1947
Who holds an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card
Who himself/herself, either parent, or any grandparent was born in undivided India
Who has lived in India for at least 10 years at any point in their lifetime

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series X-B (p.140), a foreign national qualifies as a Person of Indian Origin if he/she, either parent, or any grandparent was born in undivided India. The "undivided India" reference is to India as it existed before partition on 15th August 1947. The Trap: The PIO definition under the Income Tax Act is distinct from the immigration/OCI card concept. It is a specific legal test based on the person's, parents', or grandparents' birth in undivided India — not merely on holding an OCI card or having lived in India for a number of years. Note: PIO status affects the day-count thresholds used to determine residential status under the Income Tax Act; verify birth records of the client and their parents/grandparents during onboarding of NRI clients.
